# Extension map: the layering ADR and the audit of the core
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #141, sha256:3fad2b1cdafd22cbd510818c92ea68a565e73b884c4f5727b4029f0ee8dc8541). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** docs (thin slice; an ADR and an audit, no code)
- **Milestone:** Layered language: a domain-neutral core and one extension per domain
- **Source:** Steve's direction rulings relayed by Dispatch, 2026-10-28 (web keywords belong in a web extension, not the core; look for clean breaks for other domains: desktop UI, mobile, data, testing, messaging, file IO, auth, background jobs) and Decider D89 (Codex No with conditions, Grok Support-it; the conditions are adopted). Agile: build only the web extension now; other domains when a real use needs them.
- **Depends on:** 051
- **Story:** As Dana, I want one written map of what is core and what is an extension for each application domain, with an audit of the current core, so that the language grows by clean breaks instead of by accretion.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the ADR, When it is read, Then it defines the core as domain-neutral (phrases, specs with Given/When/Then, types, control and error patterns, effects as a mechanism and failure codes), defines an extension as a library with its own cheat sheet or index loaded only when a project uses it, keeps a target-language adapter orthogonal to a domain extension, and splits testing into core (Phrase's own specs) and extension (test-framework wiring, mocking, fixtures and the adapter side of spec-to-test generation)
  2. Given the audit, When it is read, Then it lists every domain-specific item still in the core with its proposed home: at least the verbs including PATCH, endpoint, responds, when handled, route parameters, the reserved name input, the HTTP 422 endpoint mapping, the diagnostics PH209, PH304, PH322, PH323, PH330, PH331 and PH333, provider and framework references in the emitter, the verbs ensure, validate, find, load, compute, save and publish, and the names Scheduler, Clock, Cancellation and Events of D21, plus the native-target coupling
  3. Given the candidate domains (web, desktop UI, mobile, data, testing frameworks, messaging, file IO, auth, background jobs), When the ADR is read, Then each is marked not built, and a rule says another domain extension is built only when a real use needs it; only web is built now
